analysis.investment_thesis: Affle is a genuinely impressive mobile programmatic platform with 45% revenue CAGR over 7 years, near-zero debt, and consistent FCF generation — the kind of capital-light compounding business Greenblatt loves in concept. But at 40x EV/EBITDA the earnings yield is barely 2.2%, and you simply cannot make Magic Formula math work at that multiple regardless of the quality.
key_strengths: 45.1% revenue CAGR and 45.3% net profit CAGR over 7 years — sustained hypergrowth is extraordinary and speaks to genuine competitive advantage in mobile ad-tech
Virtually debt-free balance sheet with INR 1,047 Cr cash (INR 82 Cr debt) — the company has optionality for further acquisitions from a position of financial strength
Consistent FCF generation (5/5 years positive); INR 266 Cr FCF in FY25 on INR 483 Cr EBIT represents ~55% FCF conversion — asset-light model is working
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~2.2% (EBIT INR 483 Cr / EV ~INR 21,750 Cr) requires a ~450% earnings increase or ~80% price decline before Magic Formula thresholds are reached
ROE of 14% and ROCE of 16.8% — decent but not exceptional for a company trading at 40x EV/EBITDA; the premium is pricing in many years of future improvement

Investing CF of -INR 572 Cr in FY24 vs OCF of INR 262 Cr suggests acquisition-driven growth; serial acquirers (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) carry integration risk and obscure organic returns
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 40.28x — even if EBITDA triples over 5 years, you'd still be paying 13x at entry; Magic Formula would need to see sub-10x for interest
Other Income of INR 94 Cr in FY25 (24% of EBIT) includes investment gains — stripping this yields a ROIC closer to 16-17%, not the 21% ex-cash estimate
Five separate programmatic acquisitions in under 7 years: growth by acquisition can mask organic ROIC deterioration and creates goodwill risk on the balance sheet
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Affle has earned its premium through exceptional execution: from INR 167 Cr revenue in FY18 to INR 2,266 Cr in FY25 with positive FCF throughout — this is rare discipline in a sector notorious for cash burning. The mobile advertising market in India and emerging markets has structural tailwinds, and Affle's multi-platform model (Appnext, Mediasmart, RevX, etc.) creates genuine diversification of revenue and technology moats around first-party consumer data.

The Magic Formula, however, is indifferent to narrative. At 40x EV/EBITDA, the earnings yield of 2.2% is roughly 5-6x below the minimum acceptable level. Greenblatt's entire methodology rests on the empirical observation that cheap + good systematically beats the market — but 'good without cheap' is just what the market already knows. ROE of 14% and ROCE of 16.8% are decent for a software company but not the 25%+ that would provide some fundamental justification for the multiple. The acquisitive growth strategy also introduces non-organic earnings that could unwind. Patient Magic Formula investors should bookmark this company and revisit if the multiple compresses to 15-18x EV/EBITDA.
